Chapter 4: The Power of Misinformation, Media, and Foreign Interference
In our digital world, information travels at lightning speed. Think back to the 2016 election—so much was happening at once, and most of us had no idea just how much influence was coming from places we never expected.
Misinformation spread everywhere, making it tough to know what was real and what was just made up. Social media turned into a battleground, with false stories and wild conspiracy theories reaching millions of people in the blink of an eye.
Imagine being part of a campaign during all of this. Attacks came nonstop—many based on twisted facts, or sometimes, complete lies. Some stories were so outrageous, you’d think nobody could possibly believe them... but they still caught on, shaping what people thought and felt. Even traditional news outlets struggled to keep up, and in the race to break stories, they sometimes ended up spreading the same false narratives.
Behind the scenes, foreign actors were working hard to create chaos and erode trust in democracy. We didn’t see just how big or sophisticated these efforts were until after the votes were counted. Fake social media accounts, targeted ads—all of it designed to turn Americans against each other and deepen divisions. The damage was real: trust in our institutions took a hit, and the country felt even more divided.
For those living it day to day, the experience was honestly overwhelming. You never knew what rumor might suddenly go viral, or how to fight back against so much negativity. The campaign team did everything they could to get the truth out there, but the sheer amount of misinformation felt impossible to overcome.
The media landscape had completely shifted. The old gatekeepers—the major news networks and newspapers—weren’t in charge anymore. Now, anyone with Wi-Fi and an opinion could shape the story, for better or worse. That meant chaos, unpredictability, and a place where the truth often lost out to whatever was the most sensational.
All of this really drives home why media literacy and critical thinking matter more than ever. Most folks don’t realize just how easily false information can change what they believe and how they act. So, the big challenge ahead? Teaching everyone how to spot misinformation, and making sure people and platforms are held accountable when they spread it.
The lessons of 2016 are still unfolding. Misinformation and foreign interference remain serious threats to democracy. Protecting the integrity of our elections isn’t something we can take for granted—it takes constant attention from all of us who care about the future of our country.
